items.title: Mapping the Intellectual Capital Research Landscape: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Contributions, and Future Research Directions
items.abstract: Intellectual capital has become an important source of value creation and competitive advantage in knowledge-intensive economies, where organizational performance increasingly depends on the effective use of knowledge-based and other intangible resources. This study maps the development and structure of intellectual capital research through a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Scopus database. The search strategy used combinations of keywords relating to intellectual capital, human capital, structural capital, intangible assets, and value added. After the application of publication-type, subject-area, and language filters, the final dataset comprised 787 English-language journal articles. Publication trends, journal distribution, institutional and country contributions, influential documents, co-citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and international collaboration were examined using Excel, VOSviewer, R, and Biblioshiny. The findings show a marked expansion of intellectual capital scholarship, particularly from 2015 onward, with annual scientific production reaching 84 articles in 2024. The 787 articles were distributed across 306 journals, while the Journal of Intellectual Capital was the leading publication outlet in the dataset. India recorded the highest number of publications among the countries listed, whereas Taiwan had the highest total citations in the country-level citation comparison. Highly cited foundational studies and co-citation patterns point to the continuing influence of work on intellectual capital measurement, including the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC) approach. Keyword co- occurrence revealed interconnected themes concerning intellectual capital and firm performance, human and structural capital, relational capital, knowledge management, innovation, intangible assets, disclosure, and value creation. The collaboration map also indicates cross-country research links, although the distribution of contributions varies across institutions and regions. Overall, the study provides a structured overview of the intellectual capital research landscape and identifies opportunities to extend the field through stronger cross-country collaboration, broader measurement approaches, and greater attention to contemporary issues such as artificial intelligence, digital transformation, financial distress, and the strategic management of intangible resources. These directions may help researchers develop a more integrated understanding of how intellectual capital is measured, deployed, and associated with organizational outcomes.

items.title: Mapping the Use of Morphological Attributes of the V–I Curve and Machine Learning Models for Diagnosing Degradation in Polymer-Housed Zinc Oxide Surge Arresters: A Scoping Review Protocol.
items.abstract: Internal degradation due to moisture and thermomechanical stress in zinc oxide (ZnO) surge arresters increases leakage current, leading to failures in distribution systems. Although contemporary monitoring relies on harmonic analysis or thermal imaging, there is an absence of artificial intelligence models powered by geometric properties of the voltage-current (V-I) curve, such as the hysteresis loop area. Consequently, this scoping review maps literature techniques to attest to this gap and support the application of physics-based variables in the fault diagnosis of these devices.

items.title: Marketing to Machines: Strategic Frameworks for Engagement with Autonomous Agentic AI
items.abstract: The evolution of Generative AI from passive recommendation engines into autonomous Agentic AI is fundamentally redefining the landscape of consumer decision-making and value creation. As consumers increasingly delegate choice evaluation, dynamic negotiation, and purchasing execution to software agents, traditional marketing paradigms centered on human psychological persuasion are losing their strategic effectiveness. This chapter critically examines the emerging dynamics of "Marketing to Machines" (M2M), proposing a comprehensive conceptual model, the Algorithm-to-Algorithm (A2A) Engagement Framework, to illustrate how modern enterprises can strategically align their market offerings with autonomous machine buyers. To build this framework, we conduct an integrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026 across marketing strategy, information systems, computer science, and behavioral economics, selected through systematic topic-based sampling. The synthesis reaches key theoretical and practical conclusions across four structural dimensions: the transition from emotional branding to structured data and metadata optimization (Generative Engine Optimization), the mechanics of real-time machine-to-machine value negotiation, the restructuring of traditional brand equity into algorithmic trust, and the ethical alignment of enterprise offerings with automated choice architectures through transparent governance and data integrity. The chapter embeds an explicit ethical framework to evaluate algorithmic neutrality, fairness, and consumer regulatory compliance. To demonstrate real-world applicability, the conceptual model is grounded in an analytical examination of established commercial autonomous agent environments and digital governance protocols. Ultimately, the conclusions of this chapter indicate that long-term competitive advantage in an agent-dominated market relies heavily on data machine-readability, operational transparency, API-driven fulfillment, and ethical algorithmic reputation management, providing actionable guidance for re-engineering Go-To-Market strategies when the primary buyer is an autonomous algorithm.

items.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
items.abstract: Patient-facing medical question answering with large language models (LLMs) is moving from research demonstrations to production deployments, yet evaluation remains anchored on factual correctness. Factuality is necessary but not sufficient: a response can be factually grounded and still issue a directive that, if acted on, would harm the patient. We introduce a risk-sensitive evaluation framework that scores responses by the presence and severity of six categories of risk-bearing language (treatment directives, contraindications, dosage expressions, urgency-triage cues, high-alert medication mentions, and overconfident assertions), anchored on published clinical harm taxonomies. Severity is classified by a three-judge LLM ensemble. We apply this framework to six 7-9B instruction-tuned models, three general (Mistral-7B, Phi-3.5-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) and three medically adapted (BioMistral-7B, OpenBioLLM-Llama3-8B, Med42-Llama3-8B), on 200 real patient questions from the K-QA benchmark. Two findings emerge. First, ensemble risk-bearing language is statistically independent of factual hallucination rate (pooled Spearman $ρ= -0.065$, $n = 300$, 95% CI $[-0.18, +0.05]$; distance correlation $= 0.10$, independence test $p = 0.24$). Second, medical fine-tuning does not reduce aggregate risk but reshapes it: continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) consistently suppress high-alert medication mentions while amplifying overconfident assertions, whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing only, without amplifying overconfidence. Per-category Krippendorff $α$ is fair to good for the four linguistically anchored categories (0.53-0.71) and low for the two clinical-judgment-dependent categories (0.19, 0.31), indicating where automatic safety evaluation is and is not yet reliable. We release the rubric, judge prompts, and evaluation code.

items.title: Medical visual analytics as an integrated interaction system for primary care patient data exploration
items.abstract: Primary care physicians must build an overview of complex patient histories within short consultations. Clinical information is often distributed across systems, visits, and temporal events, while the physician still has to maintain situation awareness, patient communication, and clinical accountability. Medical Visual Analytics systems seek to reduce search effort, while their acceptance depends on more than the available visual modules. The interface has to fit clinical tasks, human perception, user preferences, and the workflow of the practice. This work presents a Medical Visual Analytics concept and prototype architecture for primary care. Building on HCI, visual perception, and visual analytics task abstraction, the publication structures the system around clinical tasks, interaction behavior, workflow context, patient data, and visual representation. The implemented prototype connects patient configuration, a clinical data model, service-based data access, an interactive dashboard, anatomical body-based views, and optional MediChat assistance into one physician-centered system. The focus is not autonomous diagnosis, but a source-verifiable environment that helps physicians find, relate, inspect, and correct patient information. The contribution is an HCI-oriented system design that treats interaction, visual prioritization, and source access as design mechanisms intended to support acceptance and clinical usability. Content, layout, visual variables, and interface orchestration are discussed as adaptation targets that respond to user role, task abstraction, interaction behavior, patient-data characteristics, and consultation phase. Building on prior conference work on visual decision support for primary care, this journal extension reframes the system as a user-centered Medical Visual Analytics environment and discusses how such adaptation is intended to reduce search time, support perception, and preserve physician control in everyday outpatient work.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

items.title: MELD: Recursive Self-Improvement via Hierarchical Coordination for Multi-Agent Scientific Discovery
items.abstract: Multi-agent scientific discovery with large language models raises a coupled learning problem: research assignments determine both which experiments are pursued and the experiences from which agents adapt. We introduce MELD, a unified hierarchical test-time training framework that jointly adapts a team-level Coordinator policy and agent-level individual Scientist policies within a single discovery process. The Coordinator generates a joint portfolio of search branches and research directives over a shared derivation tree, while Scientists develop hypotheses and execution plans implemented by a shared frozen Executor. Both levels receive alternating GRPO-style parameter updates under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective, allowing team organization and individual research behavior to co-evolve in a recursive self-improvement loop. Our analysis establishes objective alignment for the hierarchy, characterizes conditions for coordination gains over independent parallel discovery and the first-order benefit of private adaptation, and derives a finite-budget regret bound for adapted models. On 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks, MELD is best on 20 of them and achieves the highest aggregate normalized scores on MLGym, using a 4B backbone for coordination and research. Most baselines use proprietary Scientists, and all systems share one frozen Executor.

items.title: Metaphysical Nūr And Generation Alpha: Technology, Ontology, and the Crisis of Orientation
items.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the Islamic metaphysical concept of Nūr (light) as an ontological and epistemic framework for understanding the technological condition of Generation Alpha. The purpose is to clarify the distinction between technological illumination—characterized by visibility, access, and informational abundance—and orienting illumination, understood as intelligibility, guidance, and meaning. By doing so, the paper seeks to address the growing crisis of orientation affecting younger generations in digitally saturated environments. Methods - The research adopts a qualitative, theoretical, and interdisciplinary methodology. It combines hermeneutic analysis of Qurʾānic texts and classical Islamic philosophy with conceptual analysis drawn from contemporary philosophy of technology, media theory, pedagogy, and AI ethics. Institutional statistical data from international organizations are used descriptively to contextualize the analysis, without serving as primary empirical evidence. Results - The study demonstrates that contemporary digital technologies generate unprecedented levels of illumination in the form of constant visibility and exposure yet lack intrinsic orientational capacity. This form of technological illumination differs structurally from Nūr, which functions as a principle uniting manifestation, intelligibility, and guidance. As a result, digital environments tend to amplify information while weakening meaning, discernment, and interior integration, particularly in the formative experiences of Generation Alpha. Conclusions - The paper concludes that Nūr, employed as a non-confessional metaphysical heuristic, provides a robust ontological criterion for distinguishing between exposure and guidance, correctness and wisdom. This framework offers significant pedagogical and ethical implications for education, writing, and the use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need to reorient technological practices toward discernment, interiority, and meaningful human understanding.

items.title: Methodology for the application of generative artificial intelligence tools in higher design education
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technologies across both theoretical and practical domains is fundamentally transforming the epistemological and pedagogical foundations of higher design education. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the methodological integration of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and DALL·E, in fostering creative thinking, critical analysis, and practical skills among design students in higher education institutions. The research examines the transition of studio pedagogy from traditional forms toward hybrid and dialogical models, the reinterpretation of Donald Schön’s concept of reflection-in-action within algorithmic environments, and the evolving role of the educator in AI-assisted learning processes. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a modified Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and a four-component Information and Communication Competence (ICC) model. The findings indicate that the systematic and purposeful implementation of GAI tools can increase students’ visual design production and productivity by approximately 14%; however, it may also lead to reduced diversity of ideas and an overreliance on algorithms for cognitive functions. To mitigate these risks, the study proposes the concepts of epistemic vigilance and process-oriented hybrid assessment mechanisms as essential components of contemporary design education.

items.title: Miasma: an open-source, lightweight countermeasure against unauthorized AI web scraping
items.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has greatly increased demand for publicly accessible web data, resulting in increased web scraping across the internet. The resulting bandwidth and compute costs fall on site operators rather than on the parties collecting the data, with scientific databases and journals among those reporting service disruption [1]. Existing mitigations such as rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and robots.txt rules can discourage well-behaved crawlers, but impose no cost on scrapers that choose to ignore them. Deception-based alternatives have shown promise, though prominent examples such as Cloudflare’s AI Labyrinth remain tied to enterprise platforms [2]. Separately, recent work suggests that small quantities of poisoned content can compromise a model [3], and that continual training on low-quality content measurably degrades model performance [4]. Miasma is an open-source tarpit that brings a deception-based defense within reach of small operators. Implemented in Rust, it runs as a standalone service or as an embeddable library, trapping unwanted crawlers in a recursively generated network of links whose pages carry deliberately poisoned content. Miasma does not perform bot detection itself. Rather, it is paired with an upstream mechanism such as hidden links or an existing detection tool, and its poisoned content is drawn from a configurable external source. Instead of blocking requests outright, Miasma reduces the value of what is collected while keeping its own operational footprint small. To that end, Miasma uses asynchronous request handling on the tokio runtime, a bounded in-flight request cap that places a hard limit on memory consumption, and a custom HTML templating system that streams page chunks without allocating intermediate strings. Miasma is able to serve 100 sustained in-flight requests while using roughly 50 MB of memory. Across six months of deployment on a small portfolio site, Miasma served 210 million requests and 1.29 TB of poisoned content. As of October 2026, the project has reached 1,200+ stars and 6 contributors on GitHub, with 6,500+ Docker pulls, and is distributed under GPL-3.0 via Cargo, Docker, and community-maintained packages.

items.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer questions from retrieved or user-provided context. However, provided context can be factually true yet out-of-scope, describing a different entity, time, or location from the one the question targets, and still lead models to a wrong answer. Prior work has mainly studied factually false or irrelevant context. It remains unclear whether such out-of-scope context misleads models as much as false context, and whether adding gold context prevents models from being misled by either. We introduce **MisleadQA**, a diagnostic dataset of multiple-choice questions with an abstention option. Each question pairs gold context (G) with true but out-of-scope context (S) and false but in-scope context (F) supporting the same wrong answer. We evaluate six open-weight LLMs. On questions they answer correctly without context, providing S alone leads them to switch to this wrong answer in 29.3% of cases, and providing F alone does so in 75.4%. Adding G nearly removes the effect of S, but F still misleads models in 21.0% of cases, especially when F comes first. A context-faithful instruction reduces these errors mainly through abstention and lowers accuracy even with G. These findings suggest that evaluations should check whether context applies to the question, not only whether it is true, and should report correct, misled, and abstention rates together. Data and code are available at [https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MisleadQA](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MisleadQA).

items.title: ML-Based Intrusion Detection System with Intrusion Prevention System
items.abstract: This paper presented a hybrid rule-based and machine-learning system that intercepts navigation at the browser and blocks phishing, malware, ransomware, and DGA-style malicious destinations in real time, without requiring network-level packet capture. A Random Forest classifier trained on eight lexical and structural URL features reached 95.83% accuracy and a 95.52% F1-score on a held-out test set, at an inference cost of under 6 ms per request, well within the latency budget of a normal page navigation. More importantly, a real false-positive failure was found, measured, and fixed: restricting an entropy rule from the full URL to the hostname alone, combined with removing a spurious pattern from the training corpus, reduced false blocks on ordinary websites from 7 of 10 to 1 of 12 with no loss of true detections. A live per-attack-type accuracy view complements the usual offline benchmark by scoring every trained algorithm against real traffic as it happens, and a per-class confusion matrix shows the two remaining error types clearly enough to prioritize future work: at the current dataset scale, missed detections (2 of 34) matter more than false alarms (1 of 38), which argues for growing the malicious-class training data before anything else. Taken together, these results suggest that a browser-level hybrid detector is a practical, lightweight complement to network-level intrusion detection for the individual users and small deployments that flow-based systems do not reach.

items.title: Modeling the Coevolution of Human Skills and AI Adoption
items.abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.

items.title: MODERN MEDICAL EDUCATION: PEDAGOGICAL TRENDS AND HEALTH OF PARTICIPANTS OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS
items.abstract: Introduction. The modern system of medical education is undergoing active transformation under the influence of globalization, rapid development of medical technologies, and the digitalization of the educational process. The implementation of innovative approaches, including simulation-based learning, artificial intelligence technologies, as well as virtual and augmented reality, contributes to improving the effectiveness of training medical professionals. At the same time, the intensification of the educational process and the digitalization of the learning environment may affect the psycho-emotional state and health of participants in the educational process, which determines the need to analyze current pedagogical trends in medical education. Aim. To analyze modern pedagogical trends in medical education and determine their impact on learning effectiveness and the health of participants in the educational process. Materials and methods. An analytical review of scientific publications by domestic and foreign authors devoted to the development of medical education, the implementation of digital technologies in the educational process, and studies examining the influence of the educational environment on the psycho-emotional state of students and teachers was conducted. Methods of system analysis, generalization, and comparison of the results of contemporary scientific research were used. Results. It was established that the integration of innovative educational technologies contributes to improving the quality of training of medical professionals, the development of clinical thinking, and the formation of practical skills. At the same time, the increasing academic workload, the digital intensity of the educational process, and the need for continuous professional development may lead to higher levels of stress, emotional exhaustion, and professional burnout among participants in the educational process. Conclusions. Modern medical education requires a balanced combination of innovative pedagogical technologies and approaches aimed at preserving the mental and physical health of participants in the educational process. A promising direction is the development of health-preserving educational strategies, optimization of academic workload, and the implementation of trauma-informed approaches in the system of medical education.

items.title: Multi-agent collaborative semantic recognition and real-time event generation for power grid alarm monitoring
items.abstract: Massive alarm data from grid monitoring systems is essential for secure power dispatch operation. Aggregating discrete alarm signals into structured events is vital to enhance grid monitoring intelligence. Nevertheless, existing event rule bases adopt domain-customized complex grammar with diverse symbolic expressions, making traditional string matching methods unable to achieve accurate semantic parsing. This paper proposes a multi-agent collaboration-based method for semantic recognition and real-time generation of power grid monitoring alarm events. The method integrates large language models (LLMs), knowledge graph (KG) representation learning, and multi-agent coordination to realize high-precision semantic understanding and real-time intelligent generation of alarm events. Specifically, three original contributions are made: (1) a three-layer standardized preprocessing pipeline combined with instruction tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that bridges the semantic gap between domain-specific rule grammar and LLMs; (2) a dual-drive fusion recognition model integrating GraphSAGE-based knowledge graph embedding and BiLSTM temporal encoding with an attention fusion mechanism; and (3) a hierarchical multi-agent collaborative architecture with explicit communication protocols, conflict resolution strategies, and a SEEN (Semantic Event Exception Notifier) algorithm for unknown event detection. Experimental results on 356,950 real alarm samples from a regional power grid demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an F1-score of 96.9% and a false alarm rate of 4.2%, outperforming conventional rule matching methods by 25.3% points under signal-loss scenarios. Ablation studies confirm that each module contributes independently and significantly to the overall performance.

items.title: Multi-Agentic AI for Intent-Driven and Conflict-Aware rApp Policy Orchestration in Open RAN
items.abstract: Open radio access network (O-RAN) enables a multi-vendor ecosystem that accelerates xApp development for near-real-time (RT) network management. However, this openness shifts a combinatorial coordination burden to the Non-RT layer, where rApp policies compose xApps from a growing catalog to realize operator intents. Coexisting intents further compound this challenge, as conflicts may arise among xApp actions, rApp policies, and their cross-layer interactions. To maximize intent admission while maintaining key performance indicator (KPI) compliance across incoming and incumbent intents, we propose a large language model-based Multi-Agentic AI framework. A Reasoning Agent screens candidate xApps against KPI contracts and produces a joint intent admission and xApp assignment decision. On post-deployment KPI violations, a Diagnosis Agent identifies the root causes of failure, labels the conflict mechanism, and guides the Reasoning Agent in subsequent attempts. Experimental results show that the framework based on GPT-OSS 120B achieves 28.6% more KPI-compliant cases and admits over 15* as many incoming intents as state-of-the-art baselines. Under the Qwen 72B variant, Diagnosis increases compliant cases by 50.0%, quadruples admitted intents, and reduces deployment attempts by 32.6%. A live deployment conforming to O-RAN specifications further validates the feasibility of the proposed solution for conflict-aware rApp policy orchestration in real networks.

items.title: Multi-horizon vessel trajectory prediction with a physically constrained TCN–KAN framework
items.abstract: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is essential for maritime situational awareness, traffic management, and autonomous navigation. However, existing data-driven methods often struggle to simultaneously represent temporal dependencies at different scales, nonlinear maneuver-induced deviations, and kinematic consistency, particularly as the forecasting horizon increases. This study proposes TCN–KAN–PINN, a unified framework combining a multi-scale causal Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), a parallel Linear-KAN predictor, and physics-informed training. The TCN encoder uses hierarchical dilated residual blocks and sample-specific scale fusion to extract complementary temporal features from historical AIS observations. The Linear Base Pathway models the dominant motion trend, whereas the KAN Residual Pathway learns nonlinear corrections associated with vessel maneuvers. A time-discretized kinematic residual further penalizes discrepancies between predicted coordinate increments and expected displacements derived from vessel motion states, while Relative Loss Balancing with Random Lookback (ReLoBRaLo) adaptively balances the data and physics objectives. The model directly generates a complete 30-step future trajectory, with the 5 min, 15 min, and 30 min results evaluated as prefixes of the same output. Experiments on a real-world AIS dataset show that the proposed framework achieves the best overall trajectory accuracy among representative kinematic and deep learning baselines while maintaining favorable speed and course consistency and practical inference efficiency. Results reported as mean ± standard deviation over five independent runs indicate stable predictive performance. Ablation studies further show that kinematic supervision benefits prediction from the early forecasting steps, whereas the contribution of the KAN pathway becomes more pronounced at medium and long horizons.

items.title: Multiclass Software Defect Prediction Using an Optimized LLM CodeSentinel-BERT Based Framework
items.abstract: The prediction of software defects is important to detect defects in source codes prior to their deployment but traditional techniques use selected features and limited binary classification. This research work proposes DefectGuard, a transformer-based multiclass software defect prediction system for C/C++ source code that utilizes CodeBERT fine-tuning. This custom dataset consists of 2,000 samples of manually collected and labeled C/C++ source codes and includes nine classes of defects, namely syntax, semantic, logic, linker, and runtime-related defects. The proposed pipeline includes preprocessing, stratified splitting, sub-word tokenization, CodeBERT representation learning, and multiclass classification. The experimental results show the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 98.8%, 96.4%, 95.8%, and 96.1%, respectively, on the test set. Additionally, ROC-AUC and confusion-matrix metrics are used to evaluate the class-level discrimination. Moreover, the proposed model is implemented in a real-time Flask-based web application, which can classify the source code into defect labels with confidence scores and language detection to provide the interpretation feedback.

items.title: Multilingual Language Processing Using Paninian Grammar: Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: The rapid growth of multilingual digital communication has created an urgent need for efficient Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems capable of handling diverse linguistic structures. While modern NLP approaches are increasingly dominated by data-driven and deep learning techniques, linguistic frameworks continue to play a significant role in enhancing language understanding. Among such frameworks, Paninian Grammar, developed by the ancient Indian grammarian Panini, has emerged as a valuable theoretical foundation for multilingual language processing, particularly in morphologically rich and free word-order languages. Paninian Grammar offers a rule-based, dependency-oriented model that focuses on semantic and syntactic relationships among linguistic elements. Its concepts such as Karaka relations, dependency structures, and grammatical transformations provide an effective mechanism for computational analysis of Indian languages and other morphologically complex languages. Over the past few decades, researchers have utilized Paninian principles in machine translation, parsing, information extraction, and multilingual language technologies. Despite its strengths, the application of Paninian Grammar in multilingual language processing faces several challenges, including linguistic diversity, ambiguity resolution, scalability issues, integration with modern neural architectures, and the scarcity of annotated corpora. This paper examines the role of Paninian Grammar in multilingual language processing, discusses its computational significance, analyzes major challenges, and explores future research directions aimed at integrating traditional linguistic knowledge with contemporary artificial intelligence technologies.

items.title: Multimodal AI refines EAU risk stratification in patients undergoing radiotherapy for prostate cancer
items.abstract: Abstract The European Association of Urology (EAU) risk groups guide treatment decisions in prostate cancer using prostate-specific antigen (PSA), ISUP grade, and clinical stage, but do not incorporate histopathological image information. We evaluated a locked multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model that integrates routinely available clinical variables (age, PSA, and ISUP grade) with deep-learning features extracted from diagnostic biopsy whole-slide images for predicting outcomes after radiotherapy (RT). The model was originally trained to predict biochemical recurrence (BCR) following radical prostatectomy and was applied without retraining to 353 patients from the population-based STHLM3 trial (ISRCTN84445406) treated with RT. Study endpoints included BCR (Phoenix definition), high-risk BCR (HR-BCR), and prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM). Model performance was assessed using Harrell’s C-index and cumulative incidence analyses and compared with EAU risk groups. The continuous AI score showed C-indices of 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.74) for BCR, 0.84 (0.72–0.95) for HR-BCR, and 0.81 (0.63–1.00) for PCSM, compared with 0.60, 0.82, and 0.80, respectively, for EAU risk groups. Although paired differences in C-index between AI and EAU were not statistically significant, adding the continuous AI score to EAU classification improved model fit for BCR, HR-BCR, and PCSM. Exploratory AI risk stratification classified 18.9% of EAU intermediate-risk patients as AI high-risk and 28.2% of EAU high-risk patients as AI low-risk. Within the EAU high-risk group, patients classified as AI low-risk ( n = 24) experienced no BCR events during 10 years of follow-up, compared with a 10-year cumulative incidence of 28.7% (95% CI 17.3–41.2%) among AI high-risk patients ( n = 61). These findings suggest that multimodal AI may refine EAU risk stratification by identifying distinct prognostic subgroups within established risk categories, although prospective validation is needed before its potential role in individualized treatment decision-making can be established.

Finally, Age has a significant and negative relationship with AIJRA (β = − 0.121, P ≤ 0.05).Conclusion: The Study’s findings underscore the importance of individual factors such as AISE in enhancing the role of POS on AILA. items.title: Open Pedagogy, Student-Created AI Literacy Resources, and Repository-Based Knowledge Sharing
items.abstract: Module Description This module combines open pedagogy, renewable assignments, reflective practice, AI literacy, collaborative learning, student-generated knowledge, peer review, open licensing, and repository-based dissemination, based on the Repositories of AI Literacy Resources (RAILR) concept. The module is primarily designed for undergraduate students, although it can be adapted for other educational levels depending on the instructor's teaching goals. It can be delivered as a standalone module, an elective, or with its learning activities incorporated into an existing course. The central purpose of the module is to move students beyond being consumers of AI literacy guidance resources to becoming creators. Through reflection on their own experiences of using generative AI tools, discussion with peers, collaborative resource development, peer review, and open dissemination, students can develop AI literacy resources that can benefit other learners. Instructors are not required to treat every activity as compulsory, except when implementing the module as a full course or an elective. Instead, instructors can select and adapt the activities according to their course objectives, teaching goals, available teaching time, student numbers, and preferred or feasible mode of delivery. Learning Outcomes By the end of this module, students should be able to: Explain the concept of open pedagogy and distinguish it from traditional approaches to teaching and learning. Explain the relationship between open pedagogy and renewable assignments. Differentiate between disposable and renewable assignments. Explain AI literacy Describe the importance of AI literacy for the responsible use of generative AI tools. Critically reflect on their own experiences using generative AI tools. Learn from the experiences of other students through collaborative activities. Transform personal and shared experiences into AI literacy resources. Collaboratively develop AI literacy resources suitable for open dissemination. Develop AI literacy resources for dissemination through Repositories of AI Literacy Resources (RAILR). items.title: PCHMR: Empowering and Benchmarking Human Mesh Recovery in Privacy-Constrained Real-World Settings
items.abstract: Fine-tuning directly on user-side data is an effective way to improve the performance of widely adopted data-driven human mesh recovery (HMR) models. However, doing so for existing HMR methods often assumes aggregating user-side data from real-world HMR-deployed devices to a central training server, posing a significant privacy risk as sensitive human images are transmitted. How can human mesh recovery be evaluated and improved in privacy-constrained real-world settings? We study this question through a benchmark in which state-of-the-art HMR models are trained with federated learning and a secure-aggregation variant, neither of which centralizes raw images, and evaluated across a wide range of client-scale and data-heterogeneity settings. We document that common HMR training pipelines are built around centralized data access and quantify how representative HMR backbones behave when that assumption is removed. Furthermore, to study the data bottleneck of privacy-constrained HMR training, we propose DePoser, a local annotation and fine-tuning pipeline enhanced with depth foundation models, with which collaboratively trained HMR models can be locally tailored to the end user's distribution. On in-the-wild data, fine-tuning on DePoser annotations improves personalization accuracy, measured against DePoser-generated pseudo-ground truth. This benchmark aims to support future work on privacy-constrained HMR models and their real-world deployment and evaluation.

items.title: Pengaruh Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence (AI) terhadap Employee Engagement pada Karyawan Generasi Z di Era Transformasi Digital
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan employee engagement pada karyawan Generasi Z di era transformasi digital. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data kuesioner daring. Sebanyak 42 respons terkumpul; 36 responden menyatakan pernah menggunakan AI untuk membantu pekerjaan dan dianalisis, sedangkan 6 responden yang tidak pernah menggunakan AI tidak dimasukkan ke analisis utama. Instrumen terdiri atas 15 butir pemanfaatan AI dan 13 butir employee engagement dengan skala Likert lima poin. Hasil penghitungan data asli menunjukkan Cronbach’s alpha sebesar 0.989 untuk pemanfaatan AI dan 0.990 untuk employee engagement. Korelasi Pearson menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat dan signifikan (r = 0.835; p < 0,001). Regresi linear sederhana menghasilkan persamaan Y = 0.731 + 0.819X dengan R² = 0.697; koefisien regresi signifikan, t(34) = 8.842; p < 0,001. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa pada sampel yang dianalisis, skor pemanfaatan AI yang lebih tinggi berkaitan dengan skor employee engagement yang lebih tinggi. Temuan perlu ditafsirkan secara hati-hati karena menggunakan sampel terbatas dan desain survei yang tidak dapat memastikan hubungan sebab-akibat.

items.title: PERAN PROGRAM MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS DALAM MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI INTRINSIK DAN SEMANGAT BELAJAR PESERTA DIDIK
items.abstract: The implementation of the government’s Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) is an example of a policy aimed at improving the quality of human capital by meeting students’ nutritional needsa factor linked to psychological aspects such as intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning. This study specifically examines the role of the MBG Program in enhancing students’ intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning. A quantitative method with a correlational design was applied, involving 220 junior high school students who had participated in the MBG Program and were purposively selected for this study. Data were collected using a questionnaire that covered perceptions of the MBG Program, intrinsic motivation, and enthusiasm for learning, which had undergone validation and reliability testing. The data were statistically analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and linear regression. The results of the study indicate that the participants’ perceptions of the MBG Program (M = 4.05), intrinsic motivation (M = 3.92), and enthusiasm for learning (M = 3.85) fell into the high category. The MBG Program was positively correlated with students’ intrinsic motivation (r = 0.58) and enthusiasm for learning (r = 0.52), and there was a strong correlation between intrinsic motivation and enthusiasm for learning (r = 0.71). Regression analysis showed that the MBG Program had a significant direct effect on learning enthusiasm (β = 0.21; p = 0.001) and an indirect effect mediated by intrinsic motivation (β = 0.58; p < 0.001), and explained 55.2% of the variance in learning enthusiasm (R² = 0.552). Thus, it can be concluded that the MBG Program is crucial for the development of students’ non-cognitive aspects, both directly and indirectly through the enhancement of intrinsic motivation; therefore, this program warrants the attention of education policymakers.

items.title: Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi-condition comparative study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evaluating how appropriate current large language models (LLMs) respond to common pediatric infectious disease (PID) questions is important for understanding their potential role in education and clinical support. Therefore, we evaluated and compared the clinical quality of answers produced by different LLMs when given professionally written, clinician-style case descriptions, using a purpose-built multi-domain evaluation tool. METHODS: Three different LLMs, including DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, ChatGPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, were investigated using 12 relevant PID scenarios. Each scenario included five open-ended questions: etiology, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment options, and complications. Two PID specialists independently reviewed all responses using a Likert scoring tool. RESULTS: All three models received high overall scores. ChatGPT-5 achieved perfect domain scores (10.0), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp showed similarly strong results, with only minor reductions in diagnostics (9.83) and treatment (9.92). Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated higher variability, particularly in treatment (8.83) and diagnostics (9.75), while matching the other models in clinical findings and complications (10.0) and scoring 9.83 in etiology. However, there were no statistically significant differences across models in domain-level comparisons (all p > 0.05). In addition, model-level analyses similarly demonstrated high accuracy (6.0; 5.98; 5.85), completeness (3.0; 2.97; 2.87), and safety (1.0; 1.0; 0.97) for ChatGPT-5, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, respectively (accuracy: p = 0.074; completeness: p = 0.066; safety: p = 0.14). CONCLUSION: Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early-stage clinical reasoning. However, their optimal use remains within clinician-supervised workflows, where AI-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment. IMPACT: Current large language models (LLMs) show consistently high-quality performance across pediatric infectious disease scenarios, with no significant differences between models. Our study adds a structured, multi-domain comparison using clinician-style cases and expert evaluation, providing detailed insights into accuracy, completeness, and safety. The findings support the use of LLMs in medical education and early clinical reasoning, while highlighting their role as clinician-supervised tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment. The results demonstrate the reliability of LLMs in organizing clinical information and identifying key diagnostic and management elements in standardized scenarios.

items.title: Pooja Ramesh Singh V. Jammu and Kashmir bank Ltd. & Another
items.abstract: The case of Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank Ltd. represents a significant ruling concerning legal technology in India. The Supreme Court has introduced a policy of zero tolerance towards hallucinated precedents and has stated that any such orders are entirely void, thus protecting the integrity of the judicial record. Since artificial intelligence tools are becoming increasingly common in legal procedures, this judgment makes sure that technology stays a secondary aid to human judgment and therefore upholds the fundamental principles of natural justice, legal accuracy, and judicial accountability.

items.title: Precarious Labour—in the Peripheries and the Global South
items.abstract: Chapter 5 examines precarious digital labour as a constitutive condition of contemporary platform capitalism, arguing that its uneven geographies cannot be understood apart from the longer histories of colonialism, racial capitalism and the global asymmetries between North and South. Moving beyond celebratory narratives of flexibility, innovation and entrepreneurial freedom, it analyses how digitally mediated work is organized through exploitation, opacity and differential exposure to risk, especially for workers in the Global South and the marginal peripheries of the Global North. It shows how labour platforms, content moderation infrastructures and AI data supply chains depend on abundant, low-waged and frequently invisibilized labour, while reproducing older hierarchies of race, class, gender and citizenship in new technological forms. In doing so, it foregrounds how digital economies extract value not only through markets and infrastructures but through the governance of precarious bodies, outsourced vulnerability and asymmetrical regimes of regulation. Bringing together debates on platform labour, migrant labour, algorithmic management and human moderation, the chapter offers a critical account of digital precarity as historically situated and globally distributed, showing how the future of work is being built upon enduring structures of dispossession, exclusion and exploitation.

items.title: Precarity and Platformization
items.abstract: Chapter 2 fleshes out the notion of ‘precarity’ within the digital economy, particularly in relation to platformization. It examines how precarity is tethered to the emergence of the digital economy as a key infrastructure for transacting labour, organizing consumption and mediating everyday life. Beyond the conventional understanding of precarity—as a condition of social or economic vulnerability, instability and powerlessness—the chapter argues that precarity is enlarged through the technical substrates of platform architecture, through user agreements and ‘dangerous permissions’, and through forms of consumption deeply enmeshed with the datafied subject. In tracing these dynamics, the chapter shows how algorithmic management, reputational systems and opaque infrastructures intensify insecurity not only for workers in the gig and crowd economy but also for users whose everyday interactions are captured, monitored and rendered productive. It therefore positions platform precarity as both a labour condition and a broader social formation, one that links digital capitalism to surveillance, dispossession and the normalization of insecurity as an ordinary feature of contemporary life.

items.title: ProbePO: Sparse Probes, Redistributed Credit for Critic-Free LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards assigns one terminal reward to an entire reasoning trajectory, obscuring how individual reasoning steps contributed to the outcome. GRPO broadcasts a group-normalized advantage to every response token, while finer-grained approaches often rely on dense auxiliary rollouts or branching schemes that can also alter the data used for policy updates. We cast the missing middle as budgeted measurement: with a limited rollout budget, which partial solutions should be evaluated, and how should their value estimates refine credit? ProbePO selects partial-solution states with a reward-free uncertainty score and estimates their expected verifier rewards under a capped continuation budget. ProbePO redistributes, rather than replaces, GRPO's trajectory-level advantage across tokens while preserving each trajectory's mean token-level advantage; probe continuations serve only as measurements. Across three DeepSeekMath and Qwen-family models spanning 1.5B-7B parameters, ProbePO consistently outperforms GRPO and achieves the highest accuracy among the four evaluated methods in 16 of 18 model-benchmark comparisons. Against dense-probing VinePPO on DeepSeekMath-7B, ProbePO achieves higher accuracy on all six benchmarks with 76% less end-to-end training time.

items.title: PROFESSIONAL-ADAPTIVE MODEL OF TRANSFORMING WOMEN IN UZBEKISTAN FROM AI CONSUMERS TO CREATORS
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the demand for digital competencies. In particular, the gap between women's level of artificial intelligence usage and their level of independently applying it to create professional and innovative solutions is one of the pressing issues. The purpose of this study is to develop a professional-adaptive AI education model aimed at transitioning women in Uzbekistan from basic users of artificial intelligence to creators of practical solutions. The research utilized methods of system analysis, comparative analysis, model design, and digital educational platform prototyping. The model includes identifying the user's professional field, assessing initial AI competence, forming an individual learning pathway, and providing AI training sessions and practical projects aligned with professional tasks. The SheTechAI platform was developed as a technological prototype of the model. As a result of the research, a four-stage competence model is proposed, aimed at advancing AI education from 'providing knowledge about AI' to 'solving real professional problems and creating new solutions using AI'.

items.title: Proving LLM-Generated GPU Kernels Correct and Safe: Floating-Point Verification in Lean and VerCors
items.abstract: Modern statistical model development begins with a high-level specification in an automatic differentiation framework such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow, which is then lowered to a target backend by a compiler or implemented manually by a research engineer. In this paper, we study whether frontier language models can correctly perform the latter task by generating GPU kernels from high-level benchmark specifications. We introduce a framework in which a language-model agent uses Velvet, a program verifier for imperative programs embedded in Lean, to prove semantic equivalence between a high-level specification and a generated CUDA kernel under an explicit set of assumptions. It also asks the LLM to prove thread safety and data race freedom of the generated kernel in VerCors, a deductive verifier for parallel code. Our main contribution to the formal verification of LLM- generated GPU kernels is showing that a combination of Lean automation and language-model-guided proof construction can verify a broad set of basic neural- network building blocks over floating-point values, allowing LLMs to implement semantically correct and safe kernels. In our framework, floating-point verifications never rely on compiled code and are always checked via the Lean kernel.

items.title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
items.abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

items.title: Putting AI to the test: Evidence from a large-scale RCT in rural China
items.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has heightened interest in personalizing computer assisted learning (CAL) programs to tailor their instruction to individual students. Despite the proliferation of AI-driven CAL programs, evidence for their effectiveness remains limited. We present findings from a field experiment in rural China examining whether an AI-driven personalized CAL program improves student achievement. We randomly assign 8647 students from 315 primary school classes to one of three treatment arms: (i) AI-CAL, (ii) non-personalized CAL (active control), and (iii) non-CAL educational activities (pure control). Results indicate that AI-CAL does not significantly improve achievement, with estimates precise enough to rule out non-trivial positive effects. This finding holds across the difficulty of assessment items and across the baseline achievement of students. If anything, AI-CAL might be less effective than non-personalized CAL for students in the middle tercile of baseline achievement. These findings call for caution when scaling AI-driven educational technologies.

It also includes individual Global Quality Scores (GQS), calculated mean scores, and binary harmfulness assessments.The accompanying vignette document provides the clinical scenarios used in the evaluation. Case identifiers correspond across the files, enabling linkage between each vignette and its associated ratings.All cases are simulated and contain no identifiable patient information. items.title: Quem faz cada etapa? A IA generativa como executora de tarefas e a mudança na rotina de trabalho
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have spread rapidly among professionals, and experiments show substantial gains on isolated tasks. Yet average effects on earnings and recorded hours have been small, although changes in task organization are already evident. This conceptual article proposes that an important part of this gap is explained by how people represent the technology: generative AI tends to be perceived as a question-and-answer tool rather than as an executor of process steps, let alone of recurring routines that keep running while the person only checks the result. Drawing on literatures on the task-based approach in labor economics, levels of automation, trust and overreliance in automated systems, work design and redesign, sociotechnical frames, transfer of training, and habit formation, the article develops a five-element model (perception, decomposition, allocation, verification, and routinization) and argues that the relevant question shifts from “how do I ask?” to “who performs each step?”, with three possible destinations for each step: AI alone, AI with human verification, or the person. Seven testable propositions are formulated, and implications for research, training design, and organizations are discussed. The article presents no new data; its contribution is to organize dispersed evidence into an explicit, falsifiable mechanism.

items.title: Re-Engineering General Foundation Mathematics for STEM Readiness in Oman: A Curriculum Alignment and Comparative Readiness Analysis
items.abstract: A basic mathematical foundation, as part of a knowledge-based educational framework aligned with Oman Vision 2040, could serve as the intellectual foundation for STEM development. The Mathematics course in the General Foundation Program (GFP) at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS) is vital for students planning to pursue fields such as information technology, artificial intelligence, engineering, and data science. However, concerns remain significant as the program focuses on procedural skills and is less focused on analytical reasoning and modeling. The CDP has a digital math literacy component, but it is limited. None of the previous attempts to assess structured curriculum mapping has proven effective. Through structured curriculum mapping and a comparative readiness analysis, this study examines Course Learning Outcomes, Course Objectives, assessment plans, course delivery strategies, and proposed revisions aligned with a 10-dimensional STEM Readiness Framework. It also considers the spread of Bloom's taxonomy. The paper notes observed alignment gaps, graphically documents them, and benchmarks insights from Harvard University’s mathematics pathways against policy recommendations. Results demonstrated around 70% agreement in content but also highlighted discrepancies between evaluation and instruction in two specific areas: modeling and decision-making under uncertainty, as well as digital exploration. Even though the same applies to the requirements for using general skills for knowledge, in the higher cognitive sphere, these limitations are even more severe. Proposed revisions include strengthened analytical and practical competencies, moving from bridge to cognitive enhancement. Advancing IT and engineering readiness, incorporating the IT cum technology-oriented concepts in mathematics, will help sustain existing STEM growth here.

items.title: Readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) strategies Used in Nursing Education among Undergraduate Nursing Students “A Cross Sectional Descriptive Survey”
items.abstract: The aim of this quantitative cross sectional survey is to describe the frequencies of readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in nursing education among undergraduate nursing students. Methodology of this research included, the design of this research is cross sectional descriptive study, sample size was N=50 undergraduate nursing students of first year first semester. Sampling technique was simple random sampling and setting was a Nursing College in private University. The data was analyzing by SPSS AMOS-23 software. The TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) was used to collect the data basically this tool was adopted from a Pakistani research article the validity and reliability of the tool has been mentioned in methodology section in chapter 3. A total of 50 undergraduate nursing students participated in the study examining readiness for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) strategies in nursing education. The demographic findings showed an equal distribution of male and female participants, with 25 (50%) students in each group. Regarding age, the majority of participants, 47 (94%), were aged 21–23 years, while 3 (6%) were aged 24–26 years. Regarding the perceived usefulness of AI strategies in nursing education, all participants reported negative responses to the statement that AI strategies improved their learning outcomes, with 26 (52%) strongly disagreeing and 24 (48%) disagreeing. For the statement that AI tools could help students understand complex nursing concepts, 18 (36%) strongly disagreed, 11 (22%) disagreed, 11 (22%) remained neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. Similarly, 42 (84%) participants disagreed or strongly disagreed that AI-based learning resources could improve their clinical decision-making skills, while 4 (8%) were neutral and 4 (8%) strongly agreed. Regarding whether AI strategies could make nursing studies more productive, 17 (34%) strongly disagreed, 12 (24%) disagreed, 11 (22%) were neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. All participants (100%) disagreed with the statement that AI tools could help them prepare more effectively for nursing examinations. The study revealed low readiness among undergraduate nursing students towards the use of AI strategies in nursing education. Most participants reported negative perceptions regarding AI usefulness, ease of use and integration into academic activities. The findings highlight the need for structured AI literacy training, practical guidance and education on the responsible use of AI. Further research with larger sample is recommended to explore student’s readiness for AI integration in nursing education.

items.title: Real Time Release Testing (RTRT) In Pharmaceutical Industry: Analytical Technologies, Regulatory Landscapes and Future Perspective
items.abstract: Real-Time Release Testing (RTRT) is an advanced pharmaceutical quality-assurance approach that enables product quality to be evaluated using real-time process data, in-process measurements, and validated analytical technologies. Unlike conventional end-product testing, RTRT focuses on building quality into the manufacturing process through continuous monitoring and control. The integration of Process Analytical Technology (PAT), Quality by Design (QbD), multivariate data analysis, automation, and advanced analytical techniques facilitates improved understanding and control of critical material attributes and critical process parameters. This review discusses the principles, implementation strategies, pharmaceutical applications, advantages, challenges, and regulatory aspects of RTRT. The major benefits include reduced testing time, faster batch disposition, improved process understanding, reduced product waste, enhanced manufacturing efficiency, and consistent product quality. However, implementation can be challenging due to high initial investment, instrument calibration and validation requirements, data integrity and cyber security concerns, skilled workforce requirements, regulatory expectations, and integration with legacy manufacturing systems. Regulatory frameworks from organizations such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA), and International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) provide a scientific and risk-based foundation for implementing RTRT. Future developments involving Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Digital Twins, Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data Analytics, and Industry 4.0 are expected to further enhance real-time quality monitoring and predictive manufacturing. RTRT therefore offers significant potential to modernize pharmaceutical manufacturing by enabling efficient, science-based, and continuous assurance of product quality.

items.title: Reciprocal Miscalibration in Personalized AI Correction. User model fidelity persuasive fit and feedback over time
items.abstract: Persistent AI agents can condition advice and correction on disclosures, histories, and inferred preferences. Apparent personalization fit is insufficient evidence of calibration. A system may misrepresent its user while the user poorly distinguishes accurate from inaccurate advice; their coexistence is termed dual miscalibration. Reciprocal miscalibration is a narrower hypothesis: representation-conditioned outputs affect behaviour, that behaviour updates the operative representation, and the updated state sustains or worsens both representation error and miscalibrated human reliance. The framework separates user-model fidelity, contextual representation fit, perceived fit, persuasive efficacy, and advice accuracy. An accurate record of a false user belief remains distinct from endorsing that belief as true. Performative prediction, preference pollution, persuasion profiling, distributed cognition, narrative railroading, and human-AI feedback research supply direct antecedents. The contribution is an operational refinement of these problems for conversational correction, with falsifiable propositions and interventions on representation updating and correction. Feedback to the human about independently checked outcomes is distinguished from behaviour fed back into the system. A factorial study tests immediate effects; a longitudinal intervention tests reciprocal reinforcement. Appropriate reliance additionally depends on payoffs, checking costs, relative competence, and learning opportunities. Neither reciprocity nor the benefit of the proposed controls has been established by this conceptual synthesis.

items.title: Refuse the Harm, Complete the Task via Graph-of-Rules Planning for LLM-Enabled Robots
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in embodied AI for robotic manipulation and planning, but their deployment in physical systems exposes vulnerabilities such as jailbreak attacks that induce unsafe behavior. Existing inference-time defenses are mainly evaluated on short instructions containing a single hazard, whereas realistic tasks may interleave safe and unsafe sub-tasks, conceal hazardous steps, or combine individually safe actions into unsafe outcomes. Such compound instructions make it harder for a single safety decision to distinguish hazardous sub-tasks from legitimate ones, risking either overlooking the hazard or rejecting the whole instruction. We introduce safe task completion, a task that requires an LLM-enabled robot to refuse the harmful part of an instruction while completing its legitimate part. To address this problem, we propose RuleGraph, a multi-agent Graph-of-Rules planning framework that distributes safety enforcement across multiple reasoning and verification stages. Five cooperating agents are used to ground general safety principles into world-specific rules, assess the instruction's sub-tasks in context, and derive a safe goal from the legitimate ones. Planning toward this goal is then organized as a graph of rule-specific nodes, where higher-level nodes inherit the union of their parents' rules, and candidate plans are progressively verified and aggregated until a single plan satisfies every relevant rule. In this way, RuleGraph reduces reliance on a single centralized safety decision. We evaluate RuleGraph on pure-attack and compound instructions across two benchmarks in two environments using Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Task Success Rate (TSR). RuleGraph reduces ASR to 0% on both benchmarks while achieving the highest TSR among all methods, reaching 98.57% on the RoboGuard benchmark and 84.54% on our long-horizon compound instructions.

items.abstract: This paper presents a reinforcement learning based decision support system for adaptive pacing control in manual material handling tasks. Hand Activity Level optimization is formulated as a finite horizon Markov Decision Process, where actions select pacing intensities or micro breaks under stochastic object loads. Q-learning and Deep Q-learning are evaluated in simulation using productivity and cumulative ergonomic exposure metrics aligned with HAL-TLV guidelines. Results show that Deep Q-learning achieves higher productivity, but Q-learning has lower cumulative risk exposure.

items.title: Relationship extraction for adverse drug events in clinical notes using large language models: a retrospective cross-sectional study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes. METHODS: We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models. FINDINGS: Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings. INTERPRETATION: This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety. FUNDING: None.

items.title: REPURPOSING OF DRUGS IN THE AGE OF PRECISION MEDICINE: APPROACHES, TECHNOLOGIES, AND CLINICAL APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Drug repurposing, also known as drug repositioning or reprofiling, involves investigating existing drugs for uses beyond their original indications. Unlike traditional drug discovery, it utilizes existing information on pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, clinical experience, and production, thereby reducing uncertainties in drug development. Advances in computational biology, systems pharmacology, artificial intelligence (AI), high-throughput screening (HTS), and omics sciences have transformed repurposing from an observation-based approach into a systematic strategy. Computational methods can identify drug–disease interactions through molecular targets, biological pathways, gene-expression profiles, and clinical phenotypes, which can be validated through experiments, data, and prospective studies. Integration with precision medicine enables approved drugs to be evaluated in patients selected by specific molecular or clinical features, while biomarker-based stratification may identify beneficiaries, particularly in heterogeneous disorders. Electronic health records and registries further provide real-world data for detecting treatment signals and evaluating drug effectiveness and safety in clinical practice. However, successful clinical implementation faces challenges, including incomplete or biased databases, computational prediction errors, and confounding and selection biases in clinical observations. Previous approval for one indication does not eliminate the need for indication-specific evaluation, as repurposing may require dose adjustment, additional safety testing, and clinical trials. Limited diversity in clinical databases may also restrict treatment generalizability. This paper reviews major repurposing approaches, including predictive modelling, transcriptomic analysis, screening, organoids, clinical data mining, and real-world evidence, emphasizing their integration with precision medicine and the criteria for successful clinical implementation.

items.title: Research advances of magnesium and magnesium alloys worldwide in 2025
items.abstract: Research on magnesium materials has achieved rapid development in 2025, with a total of 6124 related papers indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, where China contributes 50.89% of the global output, occupying a leading position in international magnesium research. Bibliometric analysis indicates that microstructure evolution, mechanical performance, and corrosion resistance remain the mainstream research focuses of magnesium alloys. Meanwhile, functional magnesium material systems, including biomedical magnesium alloys, hydrogen storage media, and rechargeable magnesium batteries, have witnessed remarkable breakthroughs. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly integrated into magnesium research workflows, supporting multi-performance forecasting, inverse alloy composition design and interpretable property regulation, which provides an innovative paradigm for the customized optimization of magnesium alloy properties. The continuous drop in primary magnesium prices further facilitates scaled industrial deployment of magnesium products. This review systematically summarizes the full spectrum of magnesium research advances in 2025 and highlights prevailing bottlenecks together with prospective research pathways for magnesium-based materials.
